chunks: Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamadani - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim quoted his father, on the authority of Yasir - the servant, that Ali ibn Musa al-Ridha (peace be upon him) said:

"You should not travel to any tombs other than our tombs. I have been oppressively poisoned to death and buried in a strange place. I hope the prayers of those who travel to visit my tomb are accepted and also their sins are forgiven."

key_terms.شَدُّ الرِّحَالِ: Traveling specifically for a purpose, often pilgrimage

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of traveling to visit the tomb of Imam al-Rida according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Khisal*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) establishes the theological principle of *ziyarat* (visitation) by distinguishing between general graves and the specific sanctity of the Imams' tombs, with a particular emphasis on his own resting place in Rayy. He connects his physical burial in 'exile' (*ghurba*) to his martyrdom by poison, framing the visitation as a means of spiritual intercession and divine forgiveness, a concept deeply rooted in Shia jurisprudence regarding the status of the Ahl al-Bayt.
